title: Bouncing and cyclic cosmologies: testability
bottleneck: Bouncing models replace the Big Bang singularity with a contracting phase that rebounds, avoiding inflation's initial-condition puzzles, but most bounces require violations of the null energy condition or other exotic physics, and distinctive predictions like specific non-Gaussianity patterns are hard to separate from inflationary ones.
why_it_blocks: If the universe is cyclic or bouncing, the Big Bang was not the beginning and inflation may be unnecessary; but without testable distinctions, these models remain philosophical alternatives rather than scientific competitors.
current_state: Ekpyrotic and matter-bounce scenarios make tentative predictions for the gravitational-wave background and non-Gaussianity that future CMB and interferometer experiments could probe. Ekpyrotic models predict negligible primordial gravitational waves, so a B-mode detection would rule them out while confirming inflation. Matter-bounce models instead predict a blue-tilted tensor spectrum, offering a sharp observational discriminant if sensitivity ever reaches it.
